standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the injectivity of the map on values over the object.

core_obligations: Injectivity (proof lines 1482-1483): the companion result gives injectivity of the map from the value at the object into the product over the members of the family.

Existence of the amalgamation (proof lines 1484-1500): a compatible family over the family is pulled back along the morphisms of the refinement, the induced maps on the pairwise products make the pulled back family compatible, and the sheaf condition for the refinement produces an amalgamation.

Identification of the restriction (proof lines 1501-1511): using the injectivity hypothesis at each member of the family, the author compares the restriction of the amalgamation with the originally given section on the pairwise products, which gives the desired equality by the sheaf condition.
proof_roadmap: Get injectivity from the companion result.
Pull back a compatible family along the refinement and amalgamate it there.
Use the injectivity hypothesis to identify the restriction of the amalgamation.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a presheaf satisfying the sheaf condition for a family and an injectivity condition at each member satisfies the sheaf condition for the family that the given one refines (statement lines 1462-1479). The proof is a complete argument: injectivity of the comparison map comes from the companion result (proof lines 1482-1483); a compatible family is pulled back along the divergence of the refinement and amalgamated using the sheaf condition for the refinement (proof lines 1484-1500); and the injectivity hypothesis at each member identifies the restriction of the amalgamation with the given section (proof lines 1501-1511). The non-formal content is the pullback computation and the final identification. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
